rejectedCandidates.title: Survey Exit Kit (Qualtrics-to-LimeSurvey/QuestionPro migration audit)
rejectedCandidates.reason: Recent institutional pain (University of Twente page updated 2026-09-24, Groningen 2026-09-11, UWA library guide 2026-10-20) but no evidence anyone pays for migration, a one-time need per institution, and buyers concentrated in the Netherlands and Australia outside Pisan's network (reachability 2, willingnessToPay 2).

rejectedCandidates.title: Decodability Checker for phonics programs
rejectedCandidates.reason: Paid demand exists (phonicsmaker on Flippa, about 428 subscribers) and EdWeek (2026-09-09) reports AI decodables misaligned to scope and sequence, but only one recent complaint, free tiers from LitLab and Project Read cap price, and K-12 is outside founder fit; close to the rejected 2026-10-30 phonics candidate.

rejectedCandidates.title: Department transfer-equivalency review assistant
rejectedCandidates.reason: Registrar is the natural buyer (institutional sale) and grant-subsidized AI articulation tools (CourseWise) and CollegeSource already serve it.

rejectedCandidates.title: Jupyter notebook accessibility checker for Title II
rejectedCandidates.reason: UC Berkeley's free open-source jupyterlab-a11y-checker (with CLI and optional LLM suggestions) already covers it; Jupyter Book closed its Title II issue in May 2026.

rejectedCandidates.reason: Harvard Crimson faculty survey (Sept 2026) shows instructors requiring version histories, but Grammarly Authorship, GPTZero replay and Draftback already serve it free or cheaply.

watchlist.title: Orphaned Embed Rescue (replace dead Trinket and Codeboard code embeds)
watchlist.targetCustomer: CS and computational-physics instructors, open-textbook authors and course-site maintainers whose pages embed runnable Trinket or Codeboard snippets.
watchlist.problemStatement: Trinket shut down on 2026-08-31 and Codeboard on 2026-10-31; embedded snippets in course pages and textbooks now show dead frames, Trinket export is offline, and self-hosting trinket-oss needs Docker and MongoDB with no LTI score passback.
watchlist.missedGate: competitiveGap 2 and willingnessToPay 3: free replacements (Coddy embeds, Dodona, Kita, trinket.strivemath.org) and Pickcode's paid migration exist, the need is a one-time migration, and Trinket's own shutdown is weak evidence that hosted code embeds sustain a paid business.

watchlist.title: Accommodated Exam Planner for departments
watchlist.targetCustomer: Instructors and course coordinators of large courses who must run their own extended-time and reduced-distraction exam sessions when the campus testing center is full.
watchlist.problemStatement: Testing centers triage: Berkeley DSP asks departments to cover 150%-time students and late instructors must find their own rooms and proctors; faculty call the process a logistical maze.
watchlist.missedGate: willingnessToPay 2 (no evidence departments pay for software; campuses buy Accommodate or AIM) and complianceBurden 2 (disability accommodation data).

watchlist.title: Gradebook reconciliation across PrairieLearn, Gradescope and Canvas
watchlist.targetCustomer: Instructors and coordinators of large courses that grade in several tools and post final grades to Canvas.
watchlist.problemStatement: Merging CSV exports with optional questions, per-student weight overrides and Canvas ID matching is done by hand or with homebrew scripts, and percentages come out wrong.
watchlist.missedGate: pain 3 and willingnessToPay 2; only one independent evidence page.

watchlist.title: Attempt-First Feedback Desk (AI first-pass feedback on ungraded practice with escalation to TAs)
watchlist.targetCustomer: Instructors of large CS and STEM courses who are moving homework to completion credit because of AI and have no grader budget.
watchlist.problemStatement: Homework is being de-graded, but instructors still want students to practice and get feedback; there is no grader budget, and students who used to come to office hours now go to general-purpose AI.
watchlist.missedGate: willingnessToPay 2 (instructors cite no grader budget) and competitiveGap 2 (CS50 Duck, PingPong, Gradescope AI features); risks being an AI wrapper.

watchlist.title: Alternative-grading layer for Canvas and autograders
watchlist.targetCustomer: CS and STEM instructors using specifications, standards-based or mastery grading on Canvas with PrairieLearn or Gradescope.
watchlist.problemStatement: LMSs and autograders only understand points, so instructors fake standards-based grades with zero-point assessments, hacky scripts and spreadsheets to handle learning targets, resubmission tokens and letter-grade bundles.
watchlist.missedGate: pain 3 (one GitHub RFC with 2 thumbs-up plus a position paper); total below 22.

watchlist.title: Course LLM key broker
watchlist.targetCustomer: Instructors teaching courses that use LLM APIs or coding agents without a campus AI gateway.
watchlist.problemStatement: Instructors need per-student capped API keys with model allowlists and term-end revocation; today they share keys, script OpenRouter or LiteLLM, or make students pay, and student keys leak.
watchlist.missedGate: pain 3 and willingnessToPay 2; campus gateways, Standard Compute, Anthropic per-user spend limits and OpenAI project limits are closing the gap.

runNotes.caveats: No candidate cleared the quality gate, so this file has no ideas. Eighteen candidates were scored (including three carried from the watchlist); the best scored 21 (Orphaned Embed Rescue, held back by free replacements and a one-time migration need). Saturday's focus sources (university RFP portals and job postings) mostly surfaced enterprise solicitations (LMS, syllabus management, enterprise AI platforms, TAMU-RFP-26-5082) that fail the procurement rule, and samsearch.co RFP pages were behind a Cloudflare check. The three watchlist entries carried from 2026-10-30 got no new fetched evidence: PrairieLearn issue 14717 has had no comments since 2026-04-28, and the LLM key broker search found only an April 2026 blog and university gateway docs (not fetched). Stack Exchange, G2 and Capterra were blocked, and reddit was reached only through mirrors. Because nothing qualified, the selection constraints (half educational, an instructor or institutional buyer, a Weekend MVP plus a Multi-week idea) could not be met, and Steps 5 and 6 had no ideas to research or review. Watchlist evidence URLs were fetched by this run's research subagents or carried from the 2026-10-30 file; the Pickcode migration page and the Tufts page were fetched by subagents. Two consecutive days with zero qualifying ideas suggest the recency-plus-two-independent-sources gate is binding hard on niche higher-ed problems.
